title: 15 Questions Every CISO Should Ask Before Allowing AI Pentesting in Production
content_md: AI-powered penetration testing is moving from periodic assessments to continuous, autonomous security validation. But before allowing an AI agent to test production systems, organizations must answer a critical question: How do we ensure the testing itself does not become a security incident? Traditional penetration testing relies heavily on human judgment. Experienced security professionals understand when to stop, which systems are too sensitive to test aggressively, and how to balance vulnerability discovery with operational safety. Autonomous AI agents are changing this model. They can discover assets, identify vulnerabilities, generate exploit attempts, adapt their strategies based on responses, and investigate attack paths at machine speed. This creates significant opportunities for security teams. Instead of waiting months between assessments, organizations can continuously validate their exposure to real-world attacks. However, greater autonomy introduces new risks. An AI agent that discovers a vulnerability may also trigger an unexpected application behavior, overwhelm a production service, access sensitive customer data, or move beyond its authorized testing scope.
